organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
title: Soil organic cover - Conservation Agriculture
claim: Cover crops protect soil during fallow periods, recycle nutrients, improve structure, interrupt monoculture, and increase agroecosystem biodiversity; in semi-arid systems they should use residual soil moisture.

title: AR6 WGIII Chapter 7: Agriculture, Forestry and Other Land Uses
claim: Increasing cropland soil organic matter can combine cover crops, crop rotation, agroforestry, organic amendments, reduced tillage, residue retention, and water management suited to arid conditions.

title: AR6 WGII Chapter 5: Food, Fibre and Other Ecosystem Products
claim: Agroforestry, polycultures, and hedgerows have robust co-benefits for biodiversity, carbon storage, and ecosystem services; a cited meta-analysis found roughly one-third higher soil carbon after conversion to agroforestry.

organization: Intergovernmental Science-Policy Platform on Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services
title: IPBES Core Glossary: Habitat Connectivity and Fragmentation
claim: Fragmentation divides continuous habitat into smaller isolated patches, while connectivity enables movement of organisms, pollen, propagules, nutrients, and moisture between habitats.

title: Riparian Forest Buffer
claim: Riparian tree and shrub corridors trap harmful chemicals and sediment, protect stream soils, and provide shade, detritus, and woody habitat; typical functional widths are about 15 to 100 feet and must match site conditions.

title: Plants for Riparian Buffers
claim: Riparian vegetation can remove up to 90 percent of unused nitrogen from cropland runoff; wider, diverse buffers also improve fish and wildlife habitat and corridor value.

organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
title: Management of Acid Soils
claim: Soils below pH 5.5 can create aluminium toxicity and nutrient deficiency; site-specific liming, acid-tolerant species, crop rotation, diversification, and adequate water management form an integrated response.

organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
title: State of Knowledge of Soil Biodiversity
claim: Soil organisms underpin nutrient cycling, water filtration, carbon sequestration, contaminant degradation, soil structure, and plant health, so soil and above-ground biodiversity interventions should be evaluated together.

title: Riparian Forest Buffers
claim: Riparian buffers filter nutrients, pesticides, animal waste, and sediment while stabilizing banks and creating terrestrial wildlife habitat and movement corridors.

organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
title: Agroforestry uptake and multifunctional benefits
claim: Agroforestry restores soil ecological functions, promotes biodiversity, regulates water, and reduces vulnerability to drought, pests, and disease through functional diversity.
